verdict.label: separate
verdict.why: Both functions create a CLI renderer with a similar split-footer configuration (screenMode, footerHeight, externalOutputMode, consoleMode, clearOnShutdown) and both call a `shutdown(renderer)` helper. That overlap is mostly option-object construction and reuse of a shared helper, not a repeated operation with its own contract. The surrounding logic differs. NEW manages a timeline write queue with a single-writer guard, a TTY fallback, and abort signals. EXISTING manages theming, splash screens, a footer, SIGINT attach/detach, and replay. The renderer options also differ: targetFps, kitty keyboard settings, and exitSignals. I do not see an independently repeated sub-operation that justifies a shared helper.

provider_context_limit: Claude canonical shared-operations prompt includes full candidate code, not supplemental caller files. Jev uses bounded context; source worker/coordinator inspect callers separately.
